![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14059897/assets/cbef822c90e494cbe75e4a0b4ef93b058fccdd0111ec997f13930b1dba44406d.png)

Calculate ${\int }_{C}\,\text{d}y,$ where $C={C}_{1}\cup {C}_{2}$ is the path comprising of two line segments, as shown above.
feedback.worked_solution:
The line integral of unity with respect to $y$ along a path $C$ is equal to the net change in $y$ between the terminal and initial points:

$$
{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}y={y}_{2}-{y}_{1},
$$

where ${y}_{2}$ is the $y$-coordinate of the terminal point, and ${y}_{1}$ is the $y$-coordinate of the initial point.

In our case, ${y}_{2}=0$ and ${y}_{1}=-1.$ Therefore,

$$
{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}y={y}_{2}-{y}_{1}=0-(-1)=1.
$$
